method: text patterns over file contents and file names; each hit is classed allowed_synthetic, pre_existing (the identical line is in the public base) or unexpected
not_ci_evidence: A local scan is not an assurance that the repository holds nothing private, and it is not CI: the CI evidence for this release is the GitHub Actions run of the tagged commit.
not_scanned: meaning: only the patterns above are searched; personal data or credentials in another shape are not detected
git history: not scanned for content; commit author/committer identity is checked in the release evidence, not by this scan
binary members: a member that is not valid UTF-8 is listed, not interpreted
runtime behaviour: nothing here shows what the code writes or logs when it runs

pattern_categories.email: any address; example.invalid, example.com, github.com, gitlab.com, gitlab.example.com and the GitHub noreply domain are allowed
pattern_categories.network: private IPv4 ranges, .local host names, tunnel provider names
pattern_categories.private_identifier: the maintainer's handle outside the public owner name, names of private projects used as fixtures, provenance and host names
pattern_categories.secret_shape: private-key headers and GitHub, OpenAI-style, AWS, Slack, PyPI tokens, bearer literals; reported by name, path and line, never by value
pattern_categories.structural: symbolic links, files larger than 1 MB, files that are not UTF-8, compiled/key/credential/database file names
pattern_categories.user_path: /Users/<name> and /home/<name> and C:\Users\<name> paths; placeholders (example, you, someone, private, x, y, runner) are allowed
